elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall ...", so all three limbs attach to every expiry and every termination event, not merely anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at the Company's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — the request trigger is generic and available after any expiration or termination, tracking the model language.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, return to the Company all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" — the 30-day clock runs from the termination/expiry event, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) ends "in a standard machine-readable format."

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete Company Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening trigger: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason."

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Return of all Company Data in machine-readable format within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination satisfies the export limb.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; condition does not apply, but the inserted limb (c) would satisfy it in any event.

reasons: Rule kind is 'missing' and the finding is correct: Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment, with no exit, data-return or deletion mechanics anywhere in the cited material — an insertion is the right remedy.

All six preferred elements are met in operative language by a single inserted paragraph; the preferred level is position-complete, so the fallback offer in the comment is presentational only and does not undercut the redline.

Minimality holds: the insertion adds no text outside the six checklist elements (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no audit or escrow procedure, no extra remedies), and nothing in the existing Sections 4.1 or 4.1(c) is deleted, paraphrased or reworded.

The data scope is drafted correctly for the Customer-Data element: "all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" is category-complete rather than a list of selected named data types, and the new shorthand "Company Data" is defined in place and used only within the same clause, leaving no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.

Intent is preserved: the ninety-day notice mechanic, the Termination Date definition and the eight-instalment Termination Payment survive unchanged and are not contradicted by the new obligations, which run post-termination.

Minor, non-blocking drafting point the drafter should tidy: the rationale calls this "a new Section 4.3" but the rendered paragraph carries only the heading "Transition Assistance; Return of Data." with no section number — add the 4.3 numbering so the clause slots cleanly into Section 4 for future cross-referencing.
